skill_entry.name: 14. Silent fallback where an assert belongs
skill_entry.trigger: Added under h/ or src/: (a) std::min/max/clamp of a shape or index value against a named limit (*_MAX_*, *_SIZE) or a literal; (b) a bare early exit (return, continue, break; no log or assert) on an index or count, where the fall-through hands the value to a callee that TRON_ASSERTs the same bound, or a comment within five lines names tests, 'defensive', 'just in case', 'sanity' or 'for now'; (c) `if (this != &other)` in a move assignment; (d) a sentinel branch (`== 0`, `!p`) in a function that then builds a hardware command; (e) a pause-only wait loop with no counter, deadline or debug_exit; (f) a new TRON_ASSERT on a shape or limit parameter with no placeholder.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Run the procedures.md greps on the -w diff; BASE = parent of the PR's first commit if HEAD is on main. 2. Clamp: grep the limit constant; a sibling TRON_ASSERT or a screen returning false makes a bad value unreachable; t/-only callers = nit. 3. Exit: read the next callee for TRON_ASSERT_LT; grep t/ for tests needing it (fix the fixture). 4. Self-move: grep movers. 5. Sentinel: read to the end with the value fixed; logging is no exit. 6. Wait: who clears the flag and can it be stuck; compare with worker.cpp's tx wait and h/system/mwaitx.hpp. 7. Assert: one placeholder per value. 8. Unreachable -> assert with the value; reachable -> comment says when; wait -> bounded exit.
skill_entry.question: Can a bug-free caller reach this condition? If not, why does the code clamp, return or spin here instead of asserting (or debug_exit), and when the assert fires, does the message say which value tripped it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A feature switch (`if (!enabled) return;`), a checker's success return, a null check after a lookup that fails by contract (weak_ptr::lock, find, getenv, free(nullptr)), an equality of two values, a planner filter skipping a candidate (PRs 2875, 4353: no comment). A release no-op after the callee's assert (PR 2713). A guard the author explains by history (3307621121). A self-move guard called 'just defensive coding' (2825161209): approved unchanged. A wait with counter, deadline, snapshot and timeout error (worker.cpp tx wait). An external-input or chunk bound, a bool or pointer assert, a line present at BASE. A deliberate head_size parameter in a test-only helper (3866590750): ask to document; a clamp inside still counts. Never block on a spin-wait.
skill_entry.finding_shape: should we just assert this? `<guard>` (<file:line>) <clamps | returns | spins> on <condition>, but <upstream screen | callee> already <asserts | steers> at <file:line>, so a bug-free caller never reaches it. In production a wrong <value> would quietly <be truncated | go uncounted | hang> instead of failing. Prefer TRON_ASSERT with <value> in the message (or debug_exit when a device command is half built), and fix the test fixture instead; or say in the comment that <state> is expected and when. Wait loop: no way to break out and debug_exit; does <existing backpressure> already serialize this? Assert: would be useful to print <value> as well.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal when a production path hides a wrong index, truncates a model shape or half-builds a device command: 'Prefer asserting', 'IMO we should assert at this level', 'should we just assert this, or debug_exit()? We can't meaningfully continue on with this right?'. minor for an unbounded spin and for an assert message: 'Just seems a bit dangerous, but probably a next iteration/enhancement effort', 'would be useful to print the head_size as well'. Question form with no severity word for a guard that may be defensive: 'So this is defensive/sanity guarding?', 'should we just assert this? Are there legit scenarios ...?'. He wrote 'nit' on none of the eight member comments. He states reservations on a spin-wait without requesting changes and without approving (PR 2872: one COMMENTED review, closed unmerged 2026-06-03); PR 2766 he approved at cef0fb5b64 'assuming you'll follow up on the remaining minor comments'.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at HEAD (sibling asserts, the file's other wait loops, how the function treats other invalid inputs); callers (the upstream screen, who moves the type, src/ versus t/ callers); other files (the eligibility function in h/tron/models/model.hpp, src/tron/gof.cpp asserts, h/common/assert.hpp macro, the mwaitx helpers in h/system/mwaitx.hpp, src/pos/worker.cpp tx wait); commits (git log -S for an earlier assert or a backed-out wait; gh api for a review commit the worktree lacks); runtime for the completion-path argument (write Insufficient data when hardware queue knowledge is needed).

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: silent fallback where an assert belongs

Setup for this check. When the review commit is already on main, `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself; take BASE as the parent of the PR's first commit: `FIRST=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json commits -q '.commits[0].oid'); BASE=$(git -C WT rev-parse $FIRST^)`. When the worktree lacks the review commit (`git -C WT cat-file -t HEAD` fails, as for PR 2766 cef0fb5b64 and PR 2233 4b7d03f71c), take the diff from `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/HEAD -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.diff"` or `gh pr diff N`, read a file at that commit with `gh api "repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=HEAD" --jq .content | base64 -d`, and run the flag-store and `git log -S` greps on the merged head or nearest ancestor. Every diff below uses `-w` so a re-indented line does not count as added (PR 2875 h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1666-1670 asserts show as `+` without -w). A new file needs no special case: its -U0 diff carries every line with `+`.

1. Clamps (shape a): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^(\+\+\+|@@|\+.*std::(min|max|clamp)<?[^;]*,\s*(\w+\()?([A-Z_]*(MAX|SIZE|LIMIT)[A-Z_]*|[0-9]+)\)?\);)'`. The +++ and @@ lines give the HEAD file and line of each hit (HEAD line = @@ new start + offset). Drop a chunk or batch bound in a loop (`std::min(remaining, CHUNK)`, `std::min(positions_data.size(), size_t(4))`), a counter floor (`std::max(x - 1, 0)`) and a limit on an external request field (`std::min<uint32_t>(request.logprobs, 20)`).
2. Silent exits (shape b): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E -A2 '^(\+\+\+|@@|\+ *if \(.*(<|>|<=|>=|==|!=|!\w)|\+ *return nullptr;)' | grep -E '^[0-9]+[:-](\+\+\+|@@|\+ *if .*(return|continue|break)|\+ *(return[^;]*;|continue;|break;))'`. This catches the one-line form and the form whose `return;` sits on the next line. Drop: a condition that is only an enable flag, an is_initialized() probe or a getenv/config result (`if (!enabled) return;`, `if (value == nullptr) return false;`); a branch that contains spdlog::error, TRON_ASSERT, TRON_ABORT or debug_exit (read 3 lines at HEAD); a success return in a checker; a null check after weak_ptr::lock(), find() or dynamic_cast; an equality of two values; a planner filter (`if (k < 2) continue;`). Keep a hit only if step 8 finds the callee assert or step 7 finds a tell within five lines. Positive-guard form: also grep `^\+ *if \(\w+ < \w+(\.size\(\))?( &&| \|\|)` for a write wrapped in a range test with no else branch, and read whether that write is the function's only effect.
3. Self-move guards (shape c): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*this != &other'`; then `git -C WT grep -n -E 'std::move\(.*<Type>|vector<<Type>>' HEAD -- h src`. Emit a question only; never a change request.
4. Sentinel branches (shape d): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+ *if \(\w+ == 0\)|^\+ *if \(!\w+\)'`. Keep a hit only if the enclosing function at HEAD calls a device command builder after the branch (`hardware::xfer_blocks`, `write_tx_descriptors`, `DmaQueue`, `descriptor`, a `.fields.` store): `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<start>,<end>p' | grep -n -E 'xfer_blocks|descriptor|\.fields\.|debug_exit|spdlog::error|TRON_ASSERT'`. A spdlog::error inside the branch does not clear the hit when the function keeps building the command (PR 2233 4b7d03f71c src/pos/worker.cpp:986-991 logs and continues). Drop a hit inside `#if 0`/`#endif` (disabled-code-left-in owns it; PR 2135 hwattention.hpp:765) and an if/else on a piece index with no command (PR 4353 model.hpp:2931).
5. Wait loops (shape e): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E -A3 '^\+ *(while ?\(|for ?\(;;\)|do \{)'`; keep a hit whose condition or body (the -A3 lines) reads an atomic or flag (`.load(`, `.wait(`, `in_flight`, `== false`) and whose body is only `ck_pr_stall()`, `_mm_pause()`, `mwaitx::delay_ns(` or `<view>.wait(N)` with no counter, no rdtsc deadline and no debug_exit. Do not put `ready`, `prepared` or `_done` in the loop-line pattern (a range-for over `ready_kv_plan` matches, PR 4353 model.hpp:2840). Who clears the flag: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<flag>\.store\(' HEAD -- src h`; record the thread (TX/RX worker, completion callback, prep worker) and whether it can be stuck. Earlier assert or backed-out wait: `git -C WT log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -S'<flag>' -- <file>`. The file's bounded form: `git -C WT show HEAD:src/pos/worker.cpp | grep -n 'max_checks\|deadline = \|debug_exit'` (HEAD c5d44bd86f: max_checks = 5 at :2009; PR 2766 raised it to 500 but never merged). Helpers: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'wait_for_|delay_ns' HEAD -- h/system/mwaitx.hpp` (wait_for_event :69/:74, wait_for_not_event :84/:89, wait_for_geq :99/:104, delay_ns :116; namespace tron::hardware::mwaitx, file h/system/mwaitx.hpp).
6. Assert messages (shape f): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E -A2 '^\+.*TRON_(ASSERT|ABORT)\('`. Keep a hit whose condition names a model-shape or hardware-limit parameter (head_size, head_dim, n_kv_heads, n_heads, layer, n_layers, tok_ix, an HBM address or length) and whose message has no `{` placeholder of any form (`{}` and `{:#016x}` both count). Expand a precomputed bool (`addr_valid`) into its operands before deciding; drop an assert on a bool flag, a loop position or a pointer-null test (`TRON_ASSERT(!populated, ...)`, `position < 4`). At most one finding per PR, never on a line present at BASE. `git -C WT grep -n 'define TRON_ASSERT(' HEAD -- h` shows h/common/assert.hpp:69 forwards `...` to fmt, so adding the value costs one argument.
7. Comment tells, to rank the hits: `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -i -E '^[-+].*//.*(unit tests?|test states?|defensive|just in case|sanity|prevent(s)? reuse|we will expect|for now|today|eventually|extend)'`. A tell on a removed (`-`) line counts when the clamp or guard under it is kept (PR 4007 removed `// NOTE that we will expect n_kvheads <= 8 today...` and kept the clamp); a tell removed together with the check it described does not (PR 2875 token_cache.cpp removes `check_usage` and its 'defensively' comment together).
8. Reachability for shapes a and b. Clamp: `git -C WT grep -n '<LIMIT>' HEAD -- h src`; every TRON_ASSERT line in that output is a sibling assert. The parameter-name grep `git -C WT grep -n -E 'TRON_ASSERT[A-Z_]*\(.*<param>' HEAD -- h src` is a supplement only (the hunk may spell `n_kvheads` where siblings spell `n_kv_heads`: 0 versus 2 hits at 29a39ac33e). Open the screen: `git -C WT grep -n -E '_eligible\(|is_supported\(|can_use' HEAD -- h`, read its body, record STEER (returns bool) or ASSERT. Classify the clamp's function by callers: `git -C WT grep -n '<function>(' HEAD -- h src t`; only t/ callers = test-only, reported at nit. Exit: open the callee the index enters next (`git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -A3 '<callee>(size_t'`) and record its TRON_ASSERT_LT lines; tests that depend on the guard: `git -C WT grep -n '<hook>' HEAD -- t/`.
9. Report one finding per hit with the shape, the reachability fact (screen or callee file:line), the production consequence, and the ask (assert with the value in the message | comment says the state is expected | bound plus diagnosed exit | add the value). Ask whether the guard is defensive before asking for the assert.

On PR 4007 (HEAD 29a39ac33e, BASE 21162f5568 = parent of the PR's first commit bc298be626; h/+src/ diff 52 lines, 4 files): step 1 hits h/pos/hwattention.hpp:466 (k_hwcacheblock prep_xfer), :990 (xfer_k_packed_entry, production: src/pos/hwattention.cpp:26), :1035 (xfer_k_entry, test-only: t/t_hwattention.cpp:418). Steps 2-6 give 0 hits; step 7 hits two removed-line tells (`we will expect n_kvheads <= 8 today`, `which we will extend eventually`) next to kept clamps. Step 8: `git grep HW_MAX_KV_HEADS` 19 hits; h/tron/models/model.hpp:789-795 model_shape_is_hwattn_eligible() returns bool (steer); src/tron/gof.cpp:195-196 and model.hpp:1571-1573 assert with the value. Reproduces 3866435051. The whole-file grep would add :389 and :594 `std::min(positions_data.size(), size_t(4))`, present at BASE and never commented on. At the approved head 3a8544cd35 steps 1-7 give 0 candidates: the asserts at :456-458, :693-695, :1043-1044, :1095-1096, :1144-1145 all carry `{}`.

On PR 4596 (HEAD 1430736b2a, file new): step 2 one-line form yields :145-146 (dropped: getenv), :350 `return nullptr` (token_path_span), :358/:390/:437/:448/:469/:673/:685/:719/:740/:741/:764 (dropped: enable flag, `!any`, `!ok`, is_initialized, is_safe_model_id, `!stats->enabled`), :409 (note_attn_job), :421 (note_join_wait), :429 (note_fpga_pass); the two-line form adds :382-383 (add_visits, the line Wade anchored on). The positive-guard grep adds :371-373 (note_token_path). Step 7 hits :346 'test state that never ran begin_forward', :368 'unit tests drive apply_page_range without a forward', :378 'test states that grow `attn`'. Step 8: row() at :327-329 has TRON_ASSERT_LT(worker, n_workers) and TRON_ASSERT_LT(layer, n_layers), so the compares at :382, :409 and :421 are redundant and their only effect is to hide a wrong index. Reproduces 4125033677; the author converted every guard to TRON_ASSERT in 15f355acb2 (attn_stats.hpp:354-392, :479-501) and deleted note_token_path.

On PR 2233 (review commit 4b7d03f71c, not in the worktree; read with gh api contents): step 4 hits src/pos/worker.cpp:986 `if (shard_stride == 0) { spdlog::error("Shard stride should NOT be ZERO! ...", ...); }` among 7 sentinel branches; the function then stores shard_stride into the K and V weight commands, and treats too-much-context with spdlog::error + debug_exit and the batch size with TRON_ASSERT((workreq->B == 1), ...). Reproduces 2983787051; the merged head af9438799a:955-960 has `TRON_ASSERT((shard_stride != 0), "... shard_pages {}, tok_pages {}, shard_stride {} acmd_len {}", ...)` and :971/:975 store it into kwcmd/vwcmd.fields.hbm_stride.

Silent-corpus probe (precision lens, 15 silent PR diffs): with the narrowed shape (b) and the drop rules above, PR 2875 full.hpp:1001-1004 and token_tree.cpp:22, PR 4353 model.hpp:2856 and self_attention.hpp:1406, PR 2646 util.hpp:278, PR 1722 hwattention.hpp:252/:292/:305 and PR 2135 hwattention.hpp:765 produce 0 findings.
final.widen_delta: New check; nothing in the thirteen existing checks looks at production guards, clamps, spin loops or assert messages. Checks 3 and 5 look at tests only; check 6 looks at claims. The closest neighbour is check 5's 'fix the fixture' remedy: this check adds the production-side half of codex C20 ('fix an invalid test fixture instead of adding production guards that silently hide bad state'). Widen the SKILL.md description line with 'production guards that hide a bad state where an assert belongs, unbounded waits, assert messages without the value'. Add to 'How Wade words a finding': the three-question form 'should we just assert this? Are there legit scenarios ...? Is this just a common defensive coding pattern ...?' and the two-alternative form 'should we just assert this, or debug_exit()?'. Add to Words used here: TRON_ASSERT (the project's assertion macro, active in every build because h/common/assert.hpp:3-4 undefines NDEBUG; it takes a format string plus arguments and forwards them to fmt at :69), debug_exit (the process-abort-with-diagnostics path in src/pos/driver.cpp), ck_pr_stall / mwaitx (a concurrencykit busy-wait pause / the repository's timed-wait helpers in h/system/mwaitx.hpp, namespace tron::hardware::mwaitx), screen function (a model-shape eligibility check such as model_shape_is_hwattn_eligible() that returns false and steers the model to another path instead of asserting). Add to the common setup of procedures.md: when `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself, BASE is the parent of the PR's first commit from `gh pr view N --json commits`; when the worktree lacks the review commit, read the diff and files through gh api.

quotes.quote: yes, IMO we should assert at this level because we should never reach this code if HWA can't support the model shape. We already assert in (e.g.) `gof::populate` etc (which means we can't reach this anyway, if the gof-level assert trips).
quotes.what_it_shows: The deciding argument: an upstream screen or a sibling assert makes the clamp unreachable for a bad value, so the clamp should be an assert. He cites the house convention (gof::populate asserts) as the reason.

quotes.quote: In production a wrong index would quietly go uncounted instead of failing. Prefer asserting (`row()` already asserts the same bounds, so the early return is also redundant) and fix the tests to build a correctly sized state.
quotes.what_it_shows: The production consequence stated first, the redundancy with the callee's assert as the fact, and the remedy on the test fixture rather than in production code.

quotes.quote: should we just assert this? Are there legit scenarios where we would want to 'self-move'? Is this just a common defensive coding pattern, in the case we accidentally perform such an operation?
quotes.what_it_shows: His three-question form for a guard on an impossible state: assert? legitimate caller? defensive pattern? He asks whether the guard is defensive before asking for the assert, and accepted the author's 'It's just defensive coding' (2825161209) without a change.

quotes.quote: should we just assert this, or debug_exit()? We can't meaningfully continue on with this right?
quotes.what_it_shows: The two-alternative form on a sentinel branch that logs and keeps building a device command; the merged head af9438799a converted it to TRON_ASSERT with the values in the message.

quotes.quote: Also, all of these `ck_pr_stall` loops are unbounded... no way to break out in a sane manner and at least debug_exit. Just seems a bit dangerous, but probably a 'next iteration/enhancement' effort.
quotes.what_it_shows: An unbounded wait loop is flagged for having no path to debug_exit, at minor severity and explicitly deferrable; he approved the same head the next day.

quotes.quote: would be useful to print the head_size as well
quotes.what_it_shows: An assert on a shape parameter should carry the value in its message; one-line ask, approved seven minutes later without waiting for the change. The neighbouring `position < 4` assert without a value drew no comment, so the shape is limited to shape and limit parameters.

final.precedent_note: n = 8 comments over 7 PRs (positron-ai/tron 1807, 2078, 2233, 2766 x2, 2872, 4007, 4596), 2026-01-08 to 2026-09-28. One member is partly pasted assistant text: 3342904643 (PR 2872) quotes two numbered points between '---' markers that Wade introduces with 'which I let Claude summarize for me below'; his own words there are the reservation about spin-waits, the pointer to his wrap-count fix 9e4ebd056e, 'I suppose we can land this if it's critical to get the test pipeline moving forward' and the m_star question. That member is cited only for the structural half (unbounded loop, existing backpressure question) and is not quoted. The other seven members are Wade's own words. Outcomes: PR 4007 and PR 2233 converted the guard to an assert with the value; PR 4596 converted every guard to TRON_ASSERT (15f355acb2); PR 2078 kept the self-move guard and was approved; PR 2766 was approved at cef0fb5b64 with the loops unbounded and later closed unmerged; PR 2872 was closed unmerged one day after Wade's own PR 2897 (d2ee8bac0c) landed the in_flight assert; PR 1807 was approved seven minutes after the message ask.
changes_made: Shape (b) narrowed (precision fix 1 and executability): an early exit is a hit only when the fall-through hands the index to a callee that TRON_ASSERTs the same bound, or a comment within five lines carries a tell; a bare control-flow filter is not a hit. Re-run on the silent diffs: PR 2875 full.hpp:1001-1004 / token_tree.cpp:22, PR 4353 model.hpp:2856 / self_attention.hpp:1406 and PR 2646 util.hpp:278 now give 0 findings.

Step 2 command replaced with the -w, +++/@@-carrying, two-line-aware form from the executability lens; verified on `git show 1430736b2a:h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp`: it reaches :383 (add_visits, the line Wade anchored 4125033677 on) and lists the 11 enable-flag exits that the new drop rule removes. The 'On PR 4596' record now states all 18 one-line hits and how 12 are dropped, adds :382-383, and moves :371-373 (note_token_path; draft said :369-371) to the positive-guard grep.

Added drop rules to do-not-fire: feature switch / is_initialized() / getenv, checker success return, null after weak_ptr::lock or find, equality of two values, planner filter, chunk or batch bound, external-request limit, bool or pointer assert, lines present at BASE.

Shape (f) narrowed (precision fix 4, executability): only a new assert on a shape or hardware-limit parameter; any `{` placeholder form counts (`{:#016x}` included); precomputed bools expanded; bool, loop-position and pointer asserts dropped; at most one per PR. Stops PR 1722 :252 (position < 4), :292/:305 (addr_valid with {:#016x}) and the three re-indented PR 2875 asserts; keeps 2670489106.

All diff greps now use -w (precision fix 3) and the step-1 regex requires the limit to be a whole argument (executability fix: 3 hits on the PR 4007 diff, verified: diff lines 25/33/38 = hwattention.hpp:466, :990, :1035; the draft's `[0-9]+\)` arm gave 31 arithmetic hits of 41 whole-tree).

Shape (d) grep now requires a device command builder after the branch and excludes `#if 0` blocks; a spdlog::error without an exit does not clear a (d) hit (facts P2: PR 2233 4b7d03f71c worker.cpp:986-991 logs and continues).
